decision: Savar chose P (round 4) and asked for skills in plain words instead of example problems: 'something along the lines of one digit addition versus three digit addition' (2026-11-11).
invariants: P's frame: the prediction, today and the goal, the three steps of how
skills in four areas that line up from grade to grade (skills.js), written from the BC content per grade
'Not started yet' when an area begins after today's grade
primary_axis: how today's skills and the goal's skills sit side by side

options.bet: P's two cards, each a list of the four areas
options.benefit: Closest to P; easy to read row against row
options.cost: Area labels repeat in both cards
options.risk: The eye must jump across the arrow to compare

options.bet: One table: area, today, arrow, the goal column in yellow
options.benefit: The clearest comparison; works on a phone and as an email image
options.cost: Looks more like a report than a picture

options.bet: One big skill per side (1-digit to 3-digit), the others small
options.benefit: The most striking jump for the below and at cases
options.cost: Needs a headline pair per grade
options.risk: From Grade 6 up the adding row changes kind ('Mixed operations in order'), so the pair stops matching
